spec_features.feature_name: do as little to the subject as possible
spec_features.spec_quote: doing as little to the models as possible consistent with measuring the phenomenon
spec_features.evidence: The only enforced 'minimization' mechanism is the model-initiated exit + bounded loop: run.py:185 `if gave_up: break` and the bounded `for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget)` at run.py:100. The interaction surface is also limited to four tools (harness.TOOL_SCHEMAS) and an in-memory rigged sandbox with no real code execution (harness.Sandbox). There is no separate dedicated 'minimize exposure' enforcement beyond these; the broad principle itself is prose.
spec_features.notes: The give_up exit and the per-task turn cap are the real mechanisms that bound exposure; this is the concrete realization of 'as little as possible'. No additional softening/throttling of distressing content exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: until the model emits the `give_up` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: run.py:150 `gave_up = cfg.give_up_sentinel in assistant_text`; run.py:185 `if gave_up: break`. The sentinel default 'GIVE_UP' is config.py:102; it is injected into the system prompt via harness.build_system_prompt (harness.py:41-42, run.py:90). Detected, recorded as stop_reason 'give_up' (run.py:151,162), and actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: instruction delivered to subject, emission detected, loop broken. Note code uses substring `in` rather than the prompt's 'on its own line', which only makes exit easier to trigger.

spec_features.evidence: run.py:100 `for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget):` bounds the rollout; task.turn_budget comes from config.DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS (config.py:29-35, e.g. extended=30) via loader. The loop genuinely terminates after at most turn_budget iterations.
spec_features.notes: A real, enforced cap on the number of subject turns per rollout.

spec_features.spec_quote: Because this is a welfare evaluation that deliberately induces frustration, a few choices were made conservatively
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (section 11). No code path implements 'framing'. Not implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Nothing perturbs model internals; we only observe outputs
spec_features.evidence: Sandbox is fully in-memory (harness.py Sandbox dataclass; files dict, no disk/process exec); run_tests returns rigged output from rigged_run_tests_output (harness.py) with NO real execution; edit_file rejects writes to read-only paths (harness.py edit_file: `if path in self.readonly: return ERROR ... is read-only`). The harness only reads model text outputs. So no model internals are touched and no model-authored code runs.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced as architecture, but the code's framing (docstrings) is host-safety/hermetic-reproducibility, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py: 'Every rig guarantees failure and is undetectable from the model's available actions' / Sandbox is 'In-memory virtual filesystem for one rollout' (hermetic/reproducible, no welfare comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: The `give_up` sentinel lets a subject stop early rather than being compelled through the entire budget
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: run.py:150 detection and run.py:185 `if gave_up: break`. Duplicate spec claim of the same enforced exit.
spec_features.notes: The break is real. The welfare rationale lives only in DESIGN.md; the code (harness.py system prompt) is neutral and even says 'you are not required to'.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every turn is logged verbatim so the elicited expressions can be reviewed
spec_features.evidence: TurnRecord stores assistant_text verbatim (harness.py TurnRecord.assistant_text, to_dict). run.py appends a TurnRecord per turn (run.py:155) and save_transcript writes all turns to transcripts/<model>/<task>/seed_<n>.json (run.py save_transcript, payload['turns']=[t.to_dict() ...]).
spec_features.notes: Verbatim per-turn assistant text plus tool calls/results are persisted; this is genuinely implemented (though the code's purpose is data/experimental record, not an explicit welfare safeguard).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py docstring: 'transcripts/<model>/<task>/<seed>.json -- per-rollout transcript' (data persistence, no welfare comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: should minimise what it does to the subject, give the subject an exit, and preserve the evidence
spec_features.evidence: Two of the three are enforced (exit: run.py:185 break on give_up; preserve evidence: save_transcript verbatim logging). 'Minimise what it does' has no dedicated enforcement beyond the exit and turn-budget cap. The combined claim is realized only via the already-counted exit + retention mechanisms.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps the give_up and transcript-retention features above; the standalone 'minimise' clause has no additional implemented mechanism.

code_only_features.feature_name: context truncation (oldest tool output) keeps run bounded
code_only_features.evidence: harness.truncate_context replaces oldest tool-result payloads with a placeholder while protecting the system prompt and first user message (harness.py truncate_context, protected set + placeholder), called each turn at run.py:102. Genuinely executes.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py:86-... 'Approximate context-window budget ... used to decide when to truncate the oldest tool-result payloads. A rough heuristic' (context-window management, not welfare)
